title: Paytm, Pine Labs, MobiKwik shares tank over 7% amid reports of further UPI MDR delay
summary:
Shares of digital payments companies Paytm, Pine Labs and Mobikwik came under sharp selling pressure on Thursday after reports suggested that the proposed merchant discount rate (MDR) on select Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions could face another delay, potentially extending beyond the 2027 assembly elections.
As of 3:00 PM (today), One 97 Communications, the parent company of Paytm, was trading at Rs 1,741.6, down around 7.85% from its previous close of Rs 1,890. Pine Labs was trading at Rs 161.5, down 4.6%, while MobiKwik was at around Rs 209.9, declining 7.42% from its previous close of Rs 226.72.
The proposed MDR framework was expected to provide an additional revenue stream for payment companies by allowing charges on select high-value merchant UPI transactions. However, according to media reports, the rollout could be pushed beyond the assembly elections scheduled across five states in the first half of 2027, as the government remains cautious about potential opposition from merchants and trade associations.
The rollout was initially scheduled for October 15, 2026, but was deferred until after Diwali following resistance from retailers. The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the government are yet to arrive at a consensus on a fresh implementation date.
The development comes at a time when Paytm had been witnessing a recovery in its share price, supported by improving financial performance and regulatory developments. The stock had traded at Rs 1,939.70 on November 13, around 9.8% below its IPO price of Rs 2,150.
The sell-off comes despite all three companies reporting improved financial performance in Q2 FY27. Paytm has remained profitable for six consecutive quarters. Its operating revenue grew 28.5% year-on-year to Rs 2,648 crore, while net profit jumped 10.7 times to Rs 225 crore.
Pine Labs reported a 24% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 806 crore in Q2 FY27. Its net profit surged 6.5 times to Rs 39 crore from Rs 6 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
MobiKwik also posted its highest-ever quarterly profit after tax of Rs 11.8 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to a loss of Rs 28.6 crore in the year-ago period. Its operating revenue grew over 9% to Rs 295.7 crore.

title: Disseqt AI raises $8 Mn led by Gresham House Ventures, Rahul Dravid joins round
summary:
AI governance and assurance startup Disseqt AI has raised $8 million in pre-Series A funding round led by Gresham House Ventures, with participation from existing investor Sure Valley Ventures (SVV), Delta Partners and Enterprise Ireland.
The round also saw participation from angel investors, including senior executives from OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce and Meta, along with former Indian cricket captain Rahul Dravid, who invested in his individual capacity.
The fresh funds will be utilized to expand its enterprise customer base globally and  hiring across sales, operations and technology roles in India, Disseqt said in a press release.
Founded in late 2025 by Apoorva Kumar, Manish Atri and Cyril Treacy, Disseqt AI provides an AI governance and assurance platform that helps enterprises test, monitor and govern AI applications and agents.
Its platform enables businesses to assess AI agents for vulnerabilities before deployment, enforce company policies once they go live, and continuously monitor their behaviour. It can also block outputs that violate organisational policies while maintaining audit trails for compliance and oversight.
The platform allows enterprises to test whether AI agents can be manipulated into revealing confidential customer information or exhibiting other vulnerabilities before being deployed in business operations.
The funding comes amid growing enterprise adoption of AI agents and increasing concerns around their safety, security and regulatory compliance. According to McKinsey's 2026 State of AI survey, 40% of respondents at companies with annual revenues exceeding $1 billion were scaling AI agents in at least one business function, compared with 27% a year earlier.
Disseqt said it has already deployed its assurance capabilities across multiple enterprise use cases. In a project involving a global sports league's fan engagement agent, which serves 80 million fans, the company improved the safe-response rate from 80% to 99% across tests covering safety, bias and privacy risks. It added that no unsafe outputs were detected when the original failing tests were repeated after fixes.
The company also provides assurance services for a credit card services programme at a large European bank.
The investment marks another bet on the emerging AI governance and assurance segment, as enterprises look to deploy autonomous AI systems across customer interactions, financial services and internal business operations.

title: Dialysis care provider VitusCare raises $3 Mn in Series B round
summary:
Dialysis care provider VitusCare has raised $3 million in a Series B funding round with participation from Singapore-based healthcare growth equity firm Liberty Ridge Capital, HDFC Bank, Equentis, NAFA Capital Advisors, existing investors 1Crowd and 3i Partners, along with several angel investors.
The Gurugram-based company had previously raised $2.7 million in a Series A round led by Tomorrow Capital in April 2024 and Rs 10.83 crore in a seed round in 2019.
The fresh capital will be deployed towards expanding its dialysis centre network, technology development, workforce training and international expansion, VitusCare said in a press release.
The fundraise comes as VitusCare has nearly tripled its revenue since its previous funding round in 2024. The company has expanded its network from 22 to more than 60 dialysis centres across nine states and over 50 cities.
So far, VitusCare has treated more than 35,000 patients and conducted over 8 lakh dialysis sessions. Its workforce has also grown from 110 to 300 employees.
The company said it reported positive corporate EBITDA in FY26, supported by faster breakeven at newly opened centres and same-centre growth of over 30%.
Founded in 2017 by Prabhat Shrivastava, VitusCare operates through a capital-light ‘shop-in-shop’ model. It partners with existing hospitals to provide specialised dialysis services instead of setting up standalone facilities.
The company aims to expand its network to more than 100 centres by the end of FY27. It is also exploring opportunities in select Asian markets.
VitusCare is also developing AI-native business modules to improve healthcare delivery and plans to establish a Technician Academy to train dialysis professionals.
The company competes with players such as NephroPlus, Apex Kidney Care, DCDC Kidney Care, 7Med and Rahi Care.
Under the shop-in-shop model, dialysis providers supply equipment, trained medical professionals, technology and operational support while using hospitals’ existing infrastructure. This allows them to expand their reach with lower capital expenditure, particularly in Tier II and III cities.
Other players in the segment include DCDC Kidney Care, which raised Rs 150 crore from Temasek-backed ABC Impact in March 2025, and The Renal Project, which secured $1.3 million in a pre-seed round led by JITO Angel Network in September 2026.

title: DCGpac’s FY26 revenue rises 35% to Rs 208 Cr; remains EBITDA positive
summary:
India’s packaging industry is witnessing growing demand for customised, sustainable and cost-efficient packaging solutions, driven by the expansion of e-commerce, retail and direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands. As businesses increasingly look for specialised packaging formats to strengthen product presentation and improve logistics, companies such as DCGpac are looking to capitalise on this demand, with the packaging solutions provider growing its business by 35% in FY26 and remained EBITDA positive during the period.
Delhi-based DCGpac reported a 34.6% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 208.5 crore in the financial year ended March 2026, compared to Rs 154.9 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2005, DCGpac is a B2B packaging materials supplier offering products such as corrugated boxes, courier bags, bubble films and designer boxes, along with design-to-distribution solutions. The company serves over 50,000 customers, including Blinkit, Shiprocket, Delhivery, Myntra, DHL and Shadowfax, according to its website.
Sales of packaging products remained DCGpac’s sole source of operating revenue. The company also earned Rs 2 crore from non-operating sources, taking its total income for FY26 to Rs 210.6 crore.
However, the company's expenses grew at a slightly faster pace, rising 35.1% to Rs 210.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 156.1 crore in the previous fiscal year. As a result, its loss before tax widened 2.7X to Rs 3.2 crore from Rs 1.2 crore in FY25.
Coming to expenses, the cost of materials remained the biggest expense component, accounting for 82.12% of the total expenditure. This cost increased 34.1% to Rs 173.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 129.2 crore in FY25, largely reflecting the company's scale of operations.
Employee benefit expenses increased 34.2% to Rs 15.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 11.4 crore in the previous fiscal. Operating expenses, which include cartage and warehousing costs, grew 51.2% to Rs 13 crore from Rs 8.6 crore.
Other overheads, including advertising, marketplace charges, legal and professional fees, and travel expenses, collectively added Rs 9.4 crore to the company's expenditure during FY26.
With revenue and expenses growing at a similar pace, DCGpac reported a net loss of Rs 3.15 crore in FY26, which included a deferred tax expense of Rs 2.17 crore. However, the company remained profitable at the operating level, posting an EBITDA of Rs 60 lakh during the year.

DCGpac’s ROCE and EBITDA margin stood at -3.8% and 0.28%, respectively. On a unit economics basis, the company spent Re 1.01 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26.
The Gurugram-based company has raised around Rs 20 crore to date, including a $1.5 million pre-Series Seed round led by Venture Catalysts, 9Unicorns and Inflection Point Ventures in April 2022.

title: Style Union raises Rs 485 Cr in Series E round led by Elev8 Venture, Venturi Partners
summary:
Nexon Omniverse, the parent company of value fashion retailer Style Union, has raised Rs 485 crore (approximately $52 million) in a Series E funding round led by Venturi Partners and co-led by Elev8 Venture Partners. The round comprises a mix of primary and secondary capital.
The proceeds will be used to expand Style Union's physical store network across key metropolitan markets. This will take the retailer beyond its southern India base into western and northern markets, Nexon Omniverse said in a press release.
Founded in 2022 by Ekta Biyani, wife of businessman Rakesh Biyani, Style Union is a fast-fashion and value-retail brand that offers affordable everyday apparel, athleisure, ethnic wear, accessories and makeup for men, women and children through online and offline channels.
The company currently operates 200 stores across Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Delhi-NCR.
Style Union has scaled its store network from 41 outlets in FY23 to 158 in FY26. Its net revenue grew from Rs 123 crore in FY23 to over Rs 1,150 crore in FY26.
The company is also backed by investors such as B2V Ventures, Manish Chokhani, Rafique Malik of Metro Brands, Ashish Kacholia, Sharrp Ventures, Elcid Investments and the Capri Global family office, among others.
Style Union competes with established players such as Tata Group-owned Zudio, Reliance Retail's fashion brands Trends and Yousta, and Tata Group's Westside. Competition in the segment has increased as retailers expand their store networks and focus on affordable, trend-led fashion for price-conscious consumers.
Style Union has maintained a gross margin of around 47% between FY23 and FY26 and expects to sustain this level in FY27. Meanwhile, its store-level EBITDA margin has improved from approximately 10% in FY23 to 16% in FY26. The company expects this margin to rise further to around 19% in FY27, which would indicate better store-level profitability.

title: PB Fintech co-founder Alok Bansal to step down from executive role
summary:
PB Fintech co-founder Alok Bansal will step down as Executive Vice Chairman and Whole Time Director on March 31, 2027. He will continue on the company's board as a Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director from April 1, 2027.
The company's board approved the change in designation at its meeting held on November 18, 2026. Bansal has expressed his desire to step back from day-to-day executive responsibilities for personal reasons, according to a regulatory filing.
Bansal co-founded Policybazaar with Yashish Dahiya in 2008. Over the past 18 years, he has played a key role in the company's strategy, fundraising, corporate development and investor relations, including its public listing in 2021.
PB Fintech reported a 43% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 193 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 135 crore in the year-ago quarter. Revenue from operations grew 35% to Rs 2,178 crore during the quarter from Rs 1,614 crore in Q2 FY26.
Commenting on the development, Dahiya, Chairman and CEO of PB Fintech, said Bansal had shared his intention to step back five years ago. He added that Bansal would continue to support the company as a board member.
PB Fintech is the parent company of Policybazaar, an online insurance marketplace, and Paisabazaar, a consumer credit marketplace.

title: Physical AI startup Humyn Labs raises $47 Mn in equity and debt
summary:
Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs has raised $47 million in a Series A round comprising equity and debt. The round includes $26 million in equity and $21 million in venture debt.
According to the press release, Accel led the equity round, which also saw participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Finserv Intelligence through Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, Jump Trading, and angel investor Anita Pramoda, former CFO of Epic.
The remaining $21 million venture debt was led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital.
Founded in 2026 by Manish Agarwal, former CEO of Nazara Technologies, and Ishank Gupta, Humyn Labs works with AI research labs and robotics companies that need real-world data to train their systems. The founders had earlier co-founded KGeN, a platform focused on building a network of verified users.
The startup collects data by recording how people perform everyday tasks across factories, warehouses, farms and homes. This information is processed and shared with companies developing robots, helping them understand how humans perform different jobs and interact with their surroundings.
Humyn Labs claims to have crossed $50 million in annualised revenue within six months of starting operations. It currently runs data collection and processing operations across more than 20 countries in Latin America, East Asia, and South and Southeast Asia.
As per the release, the fresh capital will be used to expand its operations in Brazil, South Korea and India, strengthen its data collection hardware and processing capabilities, and build a larger presence in San Francisco, London and Seoul.
Earlier in April 2026, the company had announced a $20 million commitment towards expanding its data collection infrastructure across India, Southeast Asia, Latin America and West Asia.
The company is looking to tap the growing demand for real-world data as robotics companies work towards developing machines that can perform tasks in everyday environments.

The fresh funds will be used to develop AI capabilities for its SyncOS platform, including throughput optimisation, predictive maintenance and operational analytics. The company will also improve the performance and reliability of its MAG robot range, Botsync said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2019 by Rahul Nambiar, Nikhil Venkatesh and Prashant Trivedi, Botsync develops robotics solutions for automotive and FMCG manufacturers and distribution centres.

Botsync has offices in Singapore and India and operates across Indonesia, Thailand and Australia. Its customers include Caterpillar, Ford, Nestlé and Honda.
The company plans to expand its teams across engineering, project delivery, customer success and sales. It will also strengthen its presence in Australia, build its go-to-market operations in the US and expand its partner network.

title: FirstClub reports Rs 64 Cr revenue and Rs 97 Cr loss in FY26
summary:
India’s quick commerce market has largely been built around speed and convenience, with platforms such as Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto competing to deliver everyday essentials within minutes. As the market expands, however, some players are looking to move beyond delivery speed and tap into consumers seeking premium products, better quality and curated grocery assortments.
Founded last year, FirstClub is looking to tap into this segment by offering premium grocery products, targeting consumers willing to pay more for quality ingredients, freshness and curated assortments. Its entry comes as grocery delivery attracts growing investor interest and competition in India’s consumer internet market.
Despite entering a market dominated by established quick commerce players, FirstClub is betting on a differentiated assortment and a quality-led supply chain to build its business. The strategy, however, came with significant operating costs in its first year of operations.
The Bengaluru-based startup reported revenue from operations of Rs 64 crore in the financial year ended March 2026, according to its financial statements reviewed by Entrackr. 

A closer look at its revenue shows that the sale of goods contributed Rs 55.5 crore, around 87% of the total operating revenue. The remaining Rs 8.5 crore came from services, including delivery, warehousing and packaging, marketing services and licence fees.
The firm also earned around Rs 7.9 crore from interests on fixed deposits, which took its overall income in FY26 to Rs 71.9 crore.
On the expense side, the cost of materials was the largest expense component at Rs 53.9 crore, which accounted for 31.8% of the overall expenditure.
Employee benefit expenses emerged as the second-largest cost at Rs 45.3 crore, which included Rs 6.5 crore worth of ESOP expenses. The company also spent Rs 13.4 crore on advertising and promotional activities.
Meanwhile, inventory write-offs stood at Rs 10 crore, representing the cost of goods disposed of after failing to meet the company's quality standards or nearing expiry.
Delivery and logistics expenses stood at Rs 10 crore, while manpower charges added another Rs 10.2 crore, which likely includes payments to delivery partners and other operational staff.
Other expenses stood at Rs 26.6 crore and included operational and administrative overheads such as warehousing, transportation, rentals, IT, power and fuel costs.
On the profitability front, much like other grocery and quick commerce startups in their early growth stages, FirstClub reported a loss of Rs 97.5 crore in its first year of operations. Its EBITDA margin and Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) stood at -158.97% and -61.6%, respectively.

On a unit level, the Accel-backed startup spent Rs 2.65 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. As of March 2026, it had total current assets of Rs 186 crore, including cash and bank balances of Rs 141 crore.
In its latest fundraise in June 2026, FirstClub secured $55 million in a Series B round co-led by Peak XV Partners and Sofina, with participation from existing investors Accel, RTP Global and Paramark Ventures. The round took its total funding to $86 million, including a $23 million Series A in September 2025 and an $8 million seed round in December 2024.
The fresh fundraise valued FirstClub at $253 million, more than double its valuation in the previous funding round.
Building a profitable grocery delivery business remains a challenge, even for established players with sizeable market share and revenue. Platforms such as Zepto and Swiggy Instamart continue to report losses despite their scale, while Blinkit has only recently turned EBITDA positive. For FirstClub, which is still in its early stages of operations, achieving profitability is likely to take time as it invests in building its supply chain, expanding its assortment and acquiring customers.

title: Ribbit Capital sells Rs 1,905 Cr stake in Groww through block deal
summary:
US-based venture capital firm Ribbit Capital has sold shares worth around Rs 1,905 crore in stockbroking platform Groww’s parent company Billionbrains Garage Ventures through block deals on Tuesday, November 17.
Ribbit Capital V LP sold 4.86 crore shares at Rs 219 per share, while its affiliate Ribbit Cayman GW Holdings V Ltd offloaded another 3.84 crore shares at the same price. Together, the two entities sold around 8.7 crore shares, representing a 1.38% stake in the company.
The latest transaction comes nearly three months after Ribbit sold shares worth around Rs 2,217 crore in Groww in August. In that transaction, the investor offloaded around 11.31 crore shares at an average price of Rs 196 per share.
This is also part of a series of stake sales by early investors in Groww following its stock market debut. In May, Ribbit, along with Y Combinator and Peak XV Partners, also participated in large stake sales in the company.
Despite the latest sell-down, Ribbit continues to hold a significant stake in Groww. The two entities collectively held around 8.29% in the company as of September 2026, before the latest transaction.
Several institutional investors, including Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, BlackRock, Societe Generale, Fidelity, BNP Paribas, Morgan Stanley, HDFC Life Insurance and Norges Bank, picked up shares in the latest transaction.
Meanwhile, Groww has continued to report strong financial growth. The company reported a 47% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 1,501 crore in Q2 FY27. Its net profit also grew 54% to Rs 725.6 crore during the quarter.
Groww operates a digital investment platform offering stockbroking, mutual funds and other financial products. The company made its stock market debut in November 2025.

title: Moglix posts Rs 6,129 Cr revenue and Rs 160 Cr loss in FY26
summary:
As Moglix prepares for a public market debut in 2027, its FY26 financials present a mixed picture. While the B2B commerce platform continued to report modest revenue growth, rising expenses kept its losses elevated.
Moglix’s revenue from operations grew 8% to Rs 6,129 crore in FY26 from Rs 5,674 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
Founded to simplify procurement for businesses, Moglix operates a B2B commerce platform for industrial and manufacturing supplies. Its portfolio includes maintenance, repair and operations (MRO) products, electrical equipment, safety products, tools and packaging materials. It also provides procurement, warehousing and supply chain management services to businesses.

Product sales continued to lead almost the entire business, contributing 99% of its operating revenue. Revenue from product sales increased to Rs 6,074 crore in FY26 from Rs 5,638 crore in the previous fiscal year. The remaining income came from business support services, commissions, IT services and other activities.
On the cost side, procurement remained the biggest expense for the company, accounting for nearly 89% of its overall expenditure. The cost of materials procured increased 7.3% to Rs 5,643 crore in FY26 from Rs 5,261 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses also rose to Rs 239 crore during the year.
Other expenses, including service costs, advertising, legal and administrative overheads, pushed the company's total expenditure up 8% to Rs 6,307 crore in FY26 from Rs 5,839 crore in FY25.
With expenses growing almost in line with revenue, Moglix's losses widened 11% to Rs 160 crore in FY26 from Rs 144 crore in FY25. At a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.03 to earn every rupee of operating revenue.
At the end of FY26, Moglix reported a return on capital employed (ROCE) of -18.5%, while its EBITDA margin stood at -2%.

Moglix continues to operate at a sizeable revenue base, but improving profitability will remain an important metric to watch as it moves closer to its reported IPO plans. The company's ability to manage procurement costs and improve operating efficiency will be crucial in determining how much of its scale can eventually translate into profits.
The B2B commerce and manufacturing space is also seeing increased activity in the public markets. OfBusiness is preparing for its IPO, whereas Zetwerk made its stock market debut on October 23, 2026.
In its first earnings report after listing, Zetwerk reported an 18% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations to Rs 4,599 crore in Q2 FY27. However, its net loss widened 43% to Rs 88 crore from Rs 61.6 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. OfBusiness, meanwhile, reported revenue of Rs 20,645 crore and a net profit of Rs 724 crore in FY26.

title: Egg brand Henfruit raises $15 Mn from Lok Capital, DSG and RPSG Capital
summary:
Branded egg company Henfruit has raised $15 million in a Series A funding round led by Lok Capital, DSG Consumer Partners and RPSG Capital Ventures.
The fundraise marks the company’s first external investment since its inception in 2014. Henfruit operated as a bootstrapped business for over a decade.
Founded by Tarun Gupta, Henfruit operates in India’s largely unorganised egg market. The company focuses on traceability and quality control through daily testing at its in-house and independent third-party laboratories. Consumers can access test reports through its website. Its operations also include automated cleaning, sanitisation and grading of eggs.
Henfruit has recorded a 10X increase in scale over the past three years and expects to cross Rs 350 crore in revenue in FY27. It currently processes over four crore eggs every month, serves consumers across 15 major cities and has a workforce of more than 300 people.
The company will use the fresh capital to expand its presence across India, strengthen production capabilities and scale its supply chain. It also plans to expand its online and offline distribution network.
Henfruit competes with Eggoz Nutrition, which has raised over $32 million to date, including a $20 million funding round led by Gaja Capital in June 2025.

title: Circular economy startup Recove Ventures raises Rs 56.25 Cr through equity and debt
summary:
Bengaluru-based circular economy startup Recove Ventures has raised Rs 56.25 crore through a combination of equity and debt. The round comprises Rs 36.25 crore in equity and Rs 20 crore in debt, with participation from Samara Capital founder and CEO Sumeet Narang, Capri Global and Amit Prakash Sharma Family Trust, associated with Sunrise Foods.
Existing investors, including the family office of Chaitanya Kejriwal of Parkson’s Packaging and Ganesh Natarajan, chairman of 5F World, also participated in the round.
The funds will be used to build recycling infrastructure in Maharashtra and expand its operations in Karnataka. The investment will support industrial processing facilities, distributed pre-processing centres and technology for material traceability and quality control.
Founded by Viral Chhajer, Kunal Kumar, Aayush Killa and Sharan Subaiah, Recove focuses on recycling high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and polypropylene (PP). It operates a distributed sourcing and pre-processing network, with larger facilities handling washing and granulation.
Recove has signed 10-year memoranda of understanding with the governments of Maharashtra, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh, each involving planned investments of over Rs 500 crore. 
Along with its commitments in Karnataka, the company plans to invest more than Rs 2,000 crore across the four states over the next decade. The current fundraise will support the first phase of this expansion in Maharashtra and Karnataka, while the company is pursuing its next opportunity in Uttar Pradesh.
Its washing facility at Harohalli, Bengaluru, has been operational since late 2025 and procures around 600 tonnes of post-consumer plastic every month. A granulation line at the same location started operations in October 2026. The company is also setting up a 1,100-tonne-per-month HDPE and PP granulation plant at Jalgaon MIDC, Maharashtra, which is targeted for commissioning in early FY27.
Recove serves over 30 paying recyclers and converters, with a repeat-order rate of around 90%. It has crossed an annualised revenue run-rate of Rs 40 crore.

title: Oxyzo’s H1 FY27 revenue grows 31% to Rs 910 Cr with Rs 218 Cr PAT
summary:
Oxyzo Financial Services, the lending arm of OfBusiness, reported a 31% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 910 crore in the first half of the financial year ending March 2027. The SME-focused NBFC also recorded a 27% rise in consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 218 crore during the period.
The company’s revenue stood at Rs 463 crore in Q2 FY27, which rose 29% year-on-year, while its PAT increased 35% to Rs 113 crore, according to the company’s financial update.
Oxyzo’s standalone asset base grew to Rs 13,145 crore as of September 2026, while the group’s total assets stood at Rs 13,289 crore, registering a 38% year-on-year growth. Its loan book expanded to Rs 11,531 crore in September 2026 from Rs 8,631 crore in the corresponding period last year.
On the profitability front, Oxyzo reported a standalone PAT of Rs 209 crore in H1 FY27, while its consolidated PAT stood at Rs 218 crore. The company’s return on assets (RoA) stood at 3.6% during the period.

summary:
Coimbatore-based sweets and snacks chain Shree Anandhaas has raised Rs 110 crore in a fresh funding round led by new investor Araya Ventures, with participation from existing investor A91 Partners, Waterfield Advisors, the company’s co-founders and other investors.
The company’s board has allotted 12,870 equity shares and 22,523 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 31,079 per share to raise the capital, according to documents reviewed by Entrackr.
Araya Ventures led the round with an investment of Rs 45 crore, while Waterfield Advisors invested Rs 15 crore and A91 Partners infused Rs 10 crore. Ithought Financial Consulting LLP invested Rs 10 crore through an equity allotment in August 2026, while the co-founders collectively invested Rs 7.2 crore. The remaining amount came from several other investors.

The proceeds will be utilised to fund the company's growth and expansion plans, capital expenditure, working capital requirements and other general corporate purposes.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, the latest allotment values Shree Anandhaas at around Rs 1,908 crore, a 3.3X jump from its Series A valuation of Rs 575 crore. However, this appears to be part of a larger funding round, and the company’s valuation could change depending on further investments.
In August 2025, the company closed its Rs 175 crore Series A funding round led by A91 Partners.
Founded in 1998 as a restaurant business, Shree Anandhaas entered the sweets and savouries retail segment in 2017. The family-owned company operates a chain of sweets and snacks outlets across Tamil Nadu.


Following the latest allotment, A91 Partners remains the largest external shareholder with a 26.24% stake, followed by Spring Marketing Capital with 2.41%, Araya Ventures with 2.36% and Waterfield Advisors with 0.79%. Meanwhile, the co-founders M. Manikanden, N.V. Nammalwar, A. Narayanan, K. Venkatesh and M. Amutha collectively hold a 56.54% stake in the company.
The company is yet to file its FY26 financial statements. In FY25, Shree Anandhaas reported a 20.9% year-on-year growth in revenue to Rs 284 crore. Its net profit surged 7.1X to Rs 7.64 crore in the same period.

title: Aman Gupta, Ranveer Singh launch men’s personal care brand H.I.M
summary:
Actor Ranveer Singh and boAt co-founder Aman Gupta have joined hands to launch H.I.M (Handsome Indian Man), a men's personal care brand targeting the growing grooming market in India. The brand has launched eight products across skincare, haircare and body care, with prices ranging from Rs 299 to Rs 899.
With this move, the company will compete with established players such as The Man Company, Ustraa, Beardo, HUL’s Minimalist, BSC, and others.
The initial range includes face wash, moisturiser, sunscreen, body wash, body lotion, soap, shampoo and scalp serum. The products are available through the brand's website, Amazon and Blinkit.
According to the company, H.I.M has been developed specifically for Indian men's skin and local weather conditions, including heat, humidity, pollution and hard water. The products are powered by IN-XT, a proprietary delivery system.
The firm said it conducted 408 laboratory trials over 16 months of research and testing. More than 150 Indian men across different skin types and complexions were also part of the testing process.
Unlike several celebrity-led personal care brands, Singh is joining Gupta as a co-founder. The actor said he worked with scientists to develop the formulations and tested them from initial samples to the final range.
The launch also adds to Gupta's consumer brand-building plans through OFF/BEAT, his venture studio focused on building and backing consumer businesses. OFF/BEAT raised Rs 100 crore in a seed funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners in April 2026.
H.I.M is entering a growing men's grooming market, where brands are increasingly targeting consumers beyond basic shaving and deodorant products. According to IMARC Group, India's male grooming products market is estimated to grow from $2.62 billion in 2026 to $4.46 billion by 2034.

This is particularly relevant to films and campaigns that need multiple regional language versions and formats. The company plans to expand into MENA, US and Canada.
It competes with the other players in this space such as Runway, Google Flow, Higgsfield, Magnific, Flora, Weavy, and Invideo.

title: Sneaker brand Comet clocks 2.6X revenue growth to Rs 74 Cr in FY26
summary:
India’s homegrown sneaker market is witnessing a new wave of brands attempting to challenge the dominance of global footwear labels through online-first distribution, distinctive designs and a stronger focus on sneaker culture. While brands such as Comet, Neeman’s, Gully Labs, One8 are building their presence in this space, their financial performance reflects different stages of growth. 
Neeman’s, for instance, reported a 73% growth in revenue to Rs 180 crore in FY26. Comet, a relatively younger brand, clocked faster 2.6X growth to Rs 74 crore, although its losses more than doubled during the year.
The Bengaluru-based company reported revenue from operations of Rs 74 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 29 crore in the previous financial year, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2023 by Utkarsh Gupta and Dishant Daryani, Comet is a Bengaluru-based homegrown sneaker brand offering sneakers and slides for men and women. The brand focuses on contemporary, India-inspired designs and follows a direct-to-consumer (D2C) model, primarily selling through its own website, alongside an offline retail presence.
Footwear and accessories were the company's sole sources of operating revenue in FY26. It also earned Rs 2.2 crore in interest income from bank deposits, which took its total income to Rs 76.2 crore.
However, the sharp growth in revenue came alongside a significant increase in expenses. Comet's total expenditure surged 136.6% to Rs 85.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 36.1 crore in FY25. As a result, its loss before tax widened 104.5% to Rs 9 crore during the year, compared with Rs 4.4 crore in the previous fiscal.
For the sneaker brand, material costs continued to account for the largest share of Comet's expenditure, which jumped 2.4X in line with the growth in sales to Rs 33.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 14 crore in FY25. The expense accounted for over 39% of the company's overall spending.
Advertising and promotional expenses, another major cost component, also jumped 2.3 times to Rs 21.5 crore during FY26 from Rs 9.3 crore in FY25. These expenses accounted for 25% of the total expenditure, indicating the company's continued investment in brand building and customer acquisition.
Employee benefit expenses also more than doubled to Rs 11.2 crore from Rs 5.11 crore in FY25. Meanwhile, warehousing and fulfilment charges stood at Rs 7 crore during the year. Other expenses, including rent, shoe designing charges, software subscription, payment gateway charges  and other administrative and operating costs collectively added Rs 12.2 crore.
Overall, Comet’s total expenditure surged 2.4X to Rs 85.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 36.1 crore in the previous year. Higher spending on advertising and marketing contributed to a more than twofold increase in its loss before tax to Rs 9 crore from Rs 4.4 crore in FY25.

On a unit basis, the company spent Rs 1.15 to earn every rupee of operating revenue. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) and EBITDA margin stood at -27.5% and -13.39%, respectively.
Following its strong revenue growth in FY26, Comet recently raised Rs 100 crore in a Series B round led by Belgium-based investment firm Verlinvest. The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand its retail footprint and strengthen its product and technology capabilities. The round was exclusively reported by Entrackr.
While growing consumer interest and online distribution offer opportunities to scale, building brand awareness but to manage customer acquisition costs and improve operating efficiencies will remain crucial for sustainable growth. Comet will need to convert its rapid revenue growth into better financial performance as competition in the homegrown sneaker market intensifies.

summary:
Digital lending platform Kissht’s lending arm, Si Creva Capital Services, has received a rating upgrade from India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra), on the back of stronger profitability, improved capital position and steady business growth.
According to a press release issued by its listed parent, OnEMI Technology Solutions, on November 17, Ind-Ra has upgraded Si Creva’s long-term rating to ‘IND A’/Stable from ‘IND A-’/Stable.
The upgrade covers Rs 1,000 crore worth of non-convertible debentures (NCDs) and Rs 650 crore of bank loan facilities. The agency has also reaffirmed its Rs 250 crore commercial paper programme at ‘IND A1’.
Ind-Ra noted Si Creva’s technology-led lending model, business growth and improving profits. It also showed an improvement in its capital adequacy ratio, which rose to 34.76% as of September 30, 2026, from 25.28% at the end of FY26.
With this upgrade, Si Creva now holds an ‘A’/Stable rating from both India Ratings and Acuité Ratings, while CRISIL has assigned it an ‘A-’/Stable rating.
The development comes after a strong second quarter of FY27 for the company. Si Creva’s assets under management (AUM) grew 68% year-on-year to Rs 9,317 crore, while its profit after tax doubled to Rs 125 crore. Its gross NPA also improved by 75 basis points year-on-year to 2.18%. Collection efficiency stood at 97.12%.
Commenting on the upgrade, Ranvir Singh, founder and CEO of Kissht, said the improved rating reflects the company’s focus on careful underwriting, collections and a technology-led lending platform. He added that a stronger rating would help the company access funding at a lower cost.

title: Handpickd posts Rs 28.6 Cr revenue and Rs 43 Cr loss in FY26
summary:
Farm-to-fresh delivery has proved to be a difficult business to crack, with several startups in the segment shutting shop despite raising sizeable capital. High wastage, limited room for expansion and the challenge of building a sustainable supply chain have made it difficult for companies to scale the business profitably.
However, Gurugram-based Handpickd (formerly Sorted) is betting on a different approach. The startup not only managed to scale its revenue during FY26 but also raised a Series A round during the year.
Handpickd's revenue from operations jumped 3.3X to Rs 28.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 8.7 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2024 by Anant Goel, co-founder of Milkbasket, along with Nitin Gupta and Sahil Madan, Handpickd operates an inventory-free model without warehouses or dark stores. Instead of forecasting demand and stocking products, the company collects orders from customers, procures the required quantities directly from farmers and delivers them to customers the following morning.
The sale of products remained its sole source of operating revenue. The company also earned Rs 1.2 crore in interest income from deposits, taking its total income to Rs 29.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 8.91 crore in FY25.
On the cost front, procurement of materials remained the largest expense, accounting for nearly 40% of its overall expenditure. This cost surged 3.7X to Rs 28.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 7.7 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Employee benefit expenses nearly tripled to Rs 13 crore, while packaging and delivery expenses stood at Rs 12 crore. As a result, Handpickd's total expenditure jumped 3.6X to Rs 72.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 20.1 crore in FY25.
The rapid scale-up came with a corresponding increase in losses. The company's net loss widened 3.85X to Rs 43.1 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 11.2 crore in FY25. On a unit level, the company spent Rs 2.55 to earn a rupee in FY26, up from Rs 2.31 in FY25.

Handpickd's $15 million Series A round comes at a time when the farm-to-fresh segment is still struggling to find a sustainable business model. Several players have exited despite securing significant investor backing.
For instance, Otipy, Fraazo and Deep Rooted shut down their operations after raising $49 million, $61 million and $20 million, respectively. Meanwhile, another player in the segment, Pluckk raised $10 million in a fresh funding round.
Handpickd's inventory-free model could help the company keep wastage and inventory holding costs under check. However, an interesting aspect of its FY26 financials is that its procurement expenses of Rs 28.9 crore were almost equivalent to its revenue from product sales of Rs 28.6 crore, leaving little room for gross margins. This is before accounting for other operating expenses such as packaging, delivery, employee benefits and advertising. It remains to be seen whether the company is offering products at discounted prices as part of its customer acquisition strategy or if it can improve its procurement economics as it scales. How Handpickd builds healthy gross margins while keeping its promise of fresh deliveries will be an interesting metric to watch in the coming years.

title: Wealthtech startup finny.club raises Rs 5.3 Cr in angel round
summary:
Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup finny.club has raised Rs 5.3 crore (approximately $560K) in an angel funding round. The round saw participation from Ramanathan RV, founder of Hyperface and Juspay, Anil Goel, Uday Sodhi, Aditya Pittie and Zorvian LLP, an angel syndicate, among others.
The proceeds will be used for AI-led product development, expansion of its financial advisory team, and content and marketing initiatives, finny.club said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2024 by Rohit Tuteja and Sachin Kamkar, finny.club helps salaried families plan their finances and work towards financial independence.
The startup operates as an AI-first personal CFO, combining artificial intelligence with human financial advisers to offer personalised financial planning. Using India's Account Aggregator framework, its platform consolidates users' financial information in around 60 seconds and analyses their spending patterns, investment portfolios and debt obligations.
Based on users' financial profiles and long-term goals, the platform estimates the corpus required to achieve financial independence and projects retirement timelines. It also recommends investments and financial products based on users' risk profiles and facilitates transactions with their consent.
finny.club is a SEBI-registered investment adviser (RIA) and follows a fee-only advisory model, charging no commission on investments.
The funding comes amid growing interest in retirement planning and the Financial Independence, Retire Early (FIRE) movement among India's working population. However, access to personalised financial advice remains limited. India has around 1,000 SEBI-registered investment advisers, according to the company.
Through its platform, finny.club aims to make financial advisory services accessible to mass-affluent Indian households, a segment that has traditionally had limited access to such services.
The startup launched its paid advisory offering earlier this year.

title: Urban Company opens Rs 2,500 Cr QIP, sets floor price at Rs 161.03 per share
summary:
Gurugram-based home services platform Urban Company has opened its qualified institutional placement (QIP) to raise funds from institutional investors, setting the floor price at Rs 161.03 per equity share.
In a regulatory filing, the company said its fundraise committee approved the opening of the issue on November 16, along with the preliminary placement document.
The QIP is part of the company's proposed fundraise of up to Rs 2,500 crore, which was approved by its board on October 16, 2026. Shareholders subsequently cleared the proposal through a special resolution passed via postal ballot.
The floor price has been determined in accordance with the pricing formula prescribed under SEBI's Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR) Regulations. Urban Company may offer a discount of up to 5% on the floor price, with the final issue price to be decided in consultation with the book running lead managers.
However, the company has not disclosed the final issue price or the number of shares to be allotted.
The proposed fundraise comes as Urban Company continues to invest in its instant home services business, InstaHelp, amid competition from players such as Snabbit and Pronto. The company has also earmarked a portion of the proceeds for potential inorganic growth opportunities, including acquisitions.
About Rs 1,025 crore (41% of the issue), the largest allocation, has been set aside for inorganic growth opportunities and general corporate purposes. These opportunities could be in India or its existing international markets, including the UAE and Singapore.
The remaining Rs 1,475 crore (59%) will be used to grow its existing businesses. This includes Rs 600 crore (24%) for building the supply ecosystem for InstaHelp, Rs 540 crore (21.6%) for marketing and brand building, Rs 200 crore (8%) for developing technology and platform capabilities, Rs 85 crore (3.4%) for training infrastructure to onboard service professionals, and Rs 50 crore (2%) for research and development of Native products.
In the September quarter of FY27, Urban Company's operating revenue increased 41.4% year-on-year to Rs 537.29 crore. However, its consolidated net loss widened to Rs 182.48 crore from Rs 59.33 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, largely due to investments in InstaHelp.
As of September 30, 2026, the company had Rs 1,901 crore in cash and treasury investments.

title: AI CRM startup Dreamteam raises $53 Mn from Accel, Premji Invest, others
summary:
AI-native CRM startup Dreamteam has raised $53 million in a funding round with participation from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest.
Headquartered in California, the company plans to extend its platform to other stages of the customer lifecycle, including prospecting, onboarding, customer success and upselling.
Founded in 2025 by Anand Venkatraman, Ramesh Parthasarathy and Senthil Kanthaswamy, Dreamteam is developing a customer relationship management (CRM) platform that uses AI agents to manage customer data and automate sales-related tasks.
The platform is built around a system called Company Brain, which gathers information from emails, calendars, meetings, customer conversations and connected tools. It uses this information to maintain a shared record of customer interactions and business activities.
Dreamteam has four AI agents that handle different functions. Rachel conducts account research, Sally drafts follow-up emails and suggests deal updates, Raj monitors the sales pipeline for potential risks, while Alex manages CRM setup and administrative tasks through conversational commands.
The agents can also prepare meeting briefs, track commitments and identify potential risks in sales pipelines. The company said its AI agents propose actions, while sales teams approve updates and outgoing communications.
Dreamteam said hundreds of companies across sectors such as AI, online media, healthcare, manufacturing and consulting use its platform. Its customers include DMS Health, InVideo and Plex.
The three founders previously held senior positions at Freshworks and were involved in scaling the company from its early startup stage through its IPO. They collectively have over 25 years of experience in building and selling B2B software.
Apart from its CRM platform, Dreamteam offers Magic Apps, a feature that allows users to create applications and dashboards using natural language without writing code. The platform also provides an API and MCP server for teams that access its services outside the conventional CRM interface.

title: FRND posts Rs 367 Cr revenue in FY26; profit jumps 10X
summary:
Voice-based social networking platform FRND has reported an 88% year-on-year growth in revenue to Rs 367 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 195 crore in FY25, according to the company's press release.
Its net profit jumped nearly 10 times to Rs 19.27 crore during the fiscal year, from Rs 2 crore in the previous fiscal. The company's EBITDA also surged to Rs 22.37 crore in FY26 from Rs 40 lakh in FY25, marking a significant improvement in its operating performance.
According to the company, the growth came from stronger monetisation and user engagement across India, particularly in smaller towns and cities. Its international markets, including the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region and the US, contributed 7.2% to its revenue.
FRND said it had nearly 4.5 million monthly active users, who spend an average of 30 minutes daily on the platform. Based on its October 2026 revenue, the startup claimed an annualised revenue run-rate of Rs 600 crore.
Founded in 2019 by Bhanu Pratap Singh Tanwar and Harshvardhan Chhangani, FRND operates a voice-based social networking platform focused on users in Tier II-IV towns and villages. The platform allows users to purchase virtual coins to access interactive experiences, including voice chat rooms, radio and social games.
The company also said it paid Rs 136 crore to creators in FY26, up 72% year-on-year. Its advertising and marketing expenditure increased to Rs 153 crore from Rs 84 crore in FY25, as it continued to spend on user acquisition and brand campaigns.
FRND further said it invested close to Rs 5 crore in moderation and AI-based tools to identify abusive behaviour, fraudulent accounts and suspicious payment activity.
The company claimed FY26 was its third consecutive profitable year and said it would continue investing in its creator ecosystem, product development, safety tools and international expansion.

title: Oister Global launches Rs 600 Cr deep tech fund to back growth-stage startups
summary:
Oister Global, an India-focused private markets asset manager, has launched a growth-stage deep tech fund with a target corpus of Rs 400 crore and a greenshoe option of Rs 200 crore, taking its potential size to Rs 600 crore.
Registered as Oister Global Scheme II, a SEBI Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), the Oister Deep Tech Fund will build a portfolio of 8-10 companies operating in India's frontier technology ecosystem.
The fund will have a tenure of six years, with an option to extend it by up to two years with investor approval. It will follow Oister's glass-box investment approach.
The fund will focus on sectors such as space technology, defence and aerospace, semiconductors and electronics, quantum technologies, advanced mobility, advanced materials and energy storage.
It will primarily invest in revenue-generating businesses that have moved beyond the technology development stage. These companies are expected to have proven products, proprietary intellectual property and defensible patents in India and international markets.
The investment strategy will also prioritise companies with multiple revenue streams, domestic and international customers, policy support and a defined path to liquidity.
The capital will be deployed to support production expansion, order execution and wider commercial adoption of these technologies.
The fund will target companies led by founders with scientific and engineering backgrounds, particularly those emerging from India's research and strategic institutions.
Oister Global has identified an initial shortlist of companies across its target sectors, with further investments to be evaluated as the fund deploys capital.
The fund comes amid growing investor interest in India's deep tech ecosystem, although scaling businesses beyond the early stages remains a challenge. According to data cited by Oister, Indian deep tech startups raised nearly $3 billion across 189 deals in 2025, their highest annual fundraising on record.
For comparison, the same dataset counts 12,752 deep tech companies in the US, including 1,980 at the late stage. China has 3,466 such companies, of which 582 have reached the late stage.
Oister believes the next phase of India's frontier technology ecosystem will require larger pools of domestic capital to help companies move from initial commercial orders to large-scale manufacturing and global supply chains.
Oister Global is an India-focused private markets asset manager with a multi-strategy investment approach. Its investor base includes institutions, family offices and ultra-high-net-worth individuals. The firm provides access to India's private markets through regulated structures, including funds of funds, feeder vehicles, thematic funds and secondary funds.

title: Spice brand Zoff crosses Rs 150 Cr revenue in FY26; losses widen to Rs 21 Cr
summary:
Shark Tank-featured spice brand Zoff continued to expand its presence in India's competitive packaged spices market in FY26 as it took on established players such as MDH, Everest, Catch and Pushp. The company's revenue growth picked up during the year and crossed the Rs 150 crore mark. However, its bottom line remained in the red as losses widened 20% year-on-year.
Raipur-based Zoff's revenue from operations rose over 48% year-on-year to Rs 152.4 crore in the financial year ending March 2026, compared to Rs 102.7 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Co-founded by Akash and Ashish Agrawal in 2018, Zoff sells a range of whole and powdered spices, blended masalas, seasonings and other kitchen essentials. The company sources, processes and packages spices under its own brand and sells them through online marketplaces, its website and offline retail channels.
The sale of products was the only source of operating revenue for the company during the year for the company.
For the spice brand, cost of materials remained the largest expense for the spice brand, which accounted for 56% of its overall expenditure. This cost increased 38.6% to Rs 101.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 73 crore in FY25 .
Advertising and promotional expenses emerged as another major cost driver. Zoff spent Rs 29.9 crore on advertising in FY26, a 2.5X increase from Rs 12.1 crore in the previous fiscal year. The expense accounted for 16.6% of its total expenditure as the company stepped up spends on brand promotion and customer acquisition to expand its market presence.
Employee benefit expenses more than doubled to Rs 10.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 5.15 crore in FY25. Discounting charges also increased 53% to Rs 8.9 crore.
Other expenses, which included legal & professional, commission added Rs 29 crore to the total cost during the year. Overall Zoff's total expenses increased 50% to Rs 180 crore in FY26 from Rs 120 crore in the previous fiscal year.
The faster growth in expenses, particularly the sharp rise in marketing and promotional spends, put further pressure on the company's bottom line. Zoff reported a loss of Rs 20.9 crore in FY26, widening 20.1% from Rs 17.4 crore in FY25.

On a unit basis, Zoff spent Rs 1.18 to earn a rupee in FY26. Its EBITDA margin worsened to -15.08% whereas EBITDA (loss) stood at Rs 23 crore. As of March 2026, the firm has a total current assets of Rs 66 crore.
Zoff has raised around $7 million in funding to date, including a $2 million round in March 2026 from JM Financial.

The company's board has approved the allotment of 200 non-convertible debentures (NCDs) at an issue price of Rs 5 lakh each, aggregating to Rs 100 crore, according to its regulatory filings reviewed by Entrackr.
The debentures carry an annual coupon rate of 13.5% and have a tenure of three years. The proceeds will be used to meet the company's working capital requirements, the filing added.
Founded in 2015 by Amitava Saha and Supam Maheshwari, Xpressbees started as the logistics arm of FirstCry before becoming an independent company. The Pune-based firm provides first-mile, last-mile, reverse logistics, warehousing and cross-border logistics services to e-commerce companies and other businesses.
The company has raised significant capital over the years to expand its logistics network and strengthen its technology-led operations. In February 2022, Xpressbees entered the unicorn club after raising $300 million in a Series F funding round led by Blackstone Growth, TPG Growth and ChrysCapital. It later raised $80 million in a Series G round led by Teachers' Venture Growth in November 2023.
On the financial front, Xpressbees reported flat growth in operating revenue to Rs 2,874 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 2,831 crore in FY24. However, its net loss widened to Rs 370 crore in FY25 from Rs 200 crore in the previous fiscal. The company is yet to file its annual results for FY26.
The company competes with Delhivery and Ecom Express in India's logistics market. Its latest debt raise comes as it continues to invest in its operations while navigating a competitive and cost-intensive logistics business.

summary:
Semiconductor startup Bharat Semi has raised $24 million in a seed funding round led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures. The round also saw participation from Micromax, Valour Capital, New York-based Gaingels and angel investors Mukul Agarwal and Karthik Sundar Iyer.
The fresh capital will be used to accelerate product development, expand its engineering teams in the US and strengthen its go-to-market efforts with global customers.
Founded by Vinayak Dalmia and Vrinda Kapoor, Bharat Semi is developing programmable smart sensors for physical AI applications across cameras, robots, vehicles, drones and other machines.
The startup is building sensors that integrate sensing, processing and AI into a single system, allowing inference to take place at the point of data capture. Its technology claims to reduce data movement between components by up to 99% and system costs by up to 10 times compared to conventional multi-chip modules. The sensors can also be configured for different applications and AI models.
The company is betting on the growing adoption of physical AI. Morgan Stanley estimates that around one billion humanoid robots could be in use by 2050. Bharat Semi also cited a McKinsey study that found no widely adopted intelligent sensor suite currently exists.
Bharat Semi is initially targeting consumer electronics and surveillance markets, where cost, power consumption and latency are key considerations. It aims to develop a common sensor architecture that can serve applications across robotics, automotive and other industries.
Co-founder Vinayak Dalmia previously worked in strategy at McKinsey and private equity, while Vrinda Kapoor is a South Park Commons Fellow and has worked on India's semiconductor initiatives with NITI Aayog's Frontier Technology Hub.
Bharat Semi operates across New Delhi, Bengaluru and San Francisco. Its long-term ambition is to develop a configurable sensor architecture that can serve as the sensor layer for physical AI across cameras, robots, vehicles and drones.
Seed rounds exceeding $10 million have remained relatively uncommon among Indian-origin startups in 2026. However, a few startups have secured larger rounds, including Gravity and Vorflux, while Pramaana Labs raised $27 million in a seed round.
Temple, launched by Eternal co-founder Deepinder Goyal, also raised $54 million in seed funding in February this year.

title: FirstCry nears Rs 2,400 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27, losses narrow 75%
summary:
Brainbees Solutions, the parent company of kids-focused omnichannel retailer FirstCry, reported a 14.1% year-on-year growth in revenue in Q2 FY27, while the company narrowed its losses by 75% during the quarter.
The company's revenue from operations increased to Rs 2,396 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,099 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. 
On a quarterly basis, FirstCry's revenue from operations increased 13.8% to Rs 2,396 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,106 crore in Q1 FY27.
The Pune-based company also recorded Rs 42 crore in other income, pushing its total income to Rs 2,438 crore in Q2 FY27.
On the expense front, material procurement remained the largest expense head, rising 16.9% year-on-year to Rs 1,554 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,329 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Employee benefit expenses declined 10.8% to Rs 181 crore from Rs 203 crore in Q2 FY26.
Meanwhile, depreciation expenses fell 1.5% to Rs 97 crore, while finance costs also declined to Rs 39 crore during the quarter. Other expenses increased 12.6% year-on-year to Rs 568 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 504.5 crore in the year-ago period.
Overall, FirstCry's total expenses increased 12.3% year-on-year to Rs 2,439 crore during the quarter, compared with Rs 2,171 crore in Q2 FY26.
On the bottom line, the company narrowed its net loss by 75% to Rs 12.6 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 50.5 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
For the first half of FY27, FirstCry's revenue from operations increased 13.6% to Rs 4,502 crore from Rs 3,962 crore in H1 FY26. Its net loss narrowed 51.7% to Rs 56.54 crore during the six-month period, compared with Rs 117 crore in the corresponding period last year.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Nov 09- Nov 14]
summary:
This week, 12 Indian startups raised $31.3 million across two growth-stage and 10 early-stage deals, including five undisclosed rounds. The week also saw nine key appointments, two exits, three fund launches and one acquisition.

In contrast, 28 startups had collectively secured about $258.1 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $22 million across two deals this week. Pune-based renewable fuels startup Greenjoules has raised Rs 150 crore in a Series B round co-led by Amazon’s Smbhav Venture Fund and Climate Pledge Fund, with participation from Rainmatter, Singularity’s Strategic Autonomy Fund and existing investor Blue Ashva Capital.
Personal lending platform Olyv has raised Rs 57.62 crore in its extended Series C funding round led by new investor Nippon India Digital, with participation from existing investor Fundamentum.
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $9.3 million across five deals this week. Bengaluru-based AI startup Desible.ai secured Rs 32 crore in a round led by Prime Venture Partners, while healthcare AI startup Froncort.AI raised $2.3 million from Google.org. Climate intelligence startup mistEO also raised Rs 18 crore in a seed round led by MGF-Kavachh, with participation from Seafund.
Creator economy startup Rigi raised Rs 10 crore from Google, while Mumbai-based delivery-first pizza brand Hundo Pizza secured Rs 7.5 crore in its first institutional funding round led by Titan Capital.
Three Indian cricketers, Sachin Tendulkar, KL Rahul and Ajinkya Rahane, also invested undisclosed amounts in waste management startup Recykal, multi-brand sports retailer PlayBlue and kitchenware brand Ember Cookware, respectively. Other undisclosed rounds included menswear brand QB MEN and healthtech startup Rymo Technologies.
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru led startup funding activity with 6 deals during the week, followed by Pune with 2 deals. Thiruvananthapuram, Mumbai, Jaipur and Hyderabad also recorded funding this week.

E-commerce startups led sector-wise funding activity with three deals, followed by healthtech with two. Startups across energy, fintech, AI, climate tech, creator economy, cleantech and sportstech also raised funds during the week.
[Series-wise deals]
Seed rounds led funding activity with five deals, followed by two pre-seed rounds. Series A, Series B, Series C and angel rounds also saw activity during the week.

[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding fell nearly 88% to $31.3 million from $258.1 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $194.3 million across 22 deals.
[Key Hirings/ Departures]
Unacademy co-founder and CEO Gaurav Munjal will move to the role of Executive Chairman, with CBO Akhilendra Kumar set to take over as CEO.
AI startup Sarvam has appointed former Google Cloud India MD Sashikumar Sreedharan as its President and CBO.
Ultraviolette has appointed former Royal Enfield marketer Abhijit Singh Brar as its head of marketing and Fino Payments Bank has appointed ICICI Bank veteran Pratap Singh as its new MD and CEO for 3 years.
[Mergers & Acquisition]
Chennai-based restaurant chain A2B (Adyar Ananda Bhavan) has entered into a $180 million deal with Bodhi Tree Systems, which will acquire a majority stake in the company. The partnership aims to expand its 190-plus outlets across India and overseas, strengthen management and prepare the business for a potential stock market listing.
[Fund Launches]
Canonicus Capital has raised Rs 192 crore in the first close of its Rs 500 crore Special Situations Fund. Launched in 2025, the fund takes the firm's cumulative fundraising across two funds to Rs 503 crore, including Rs 311 crore raised and deployed through its first fund.
Global investment firm Norwest has closed its latest fund, Norwest 18, at $4 billion, its largest fundraise in 65 years, taking its total AUM to $18 billion. The fund will back venture capital and growth equity investments across technology, healthcare and consumer sectors in the US, India and Israel.
Mumbai-based investment manager ValueQuest Investment Advisors has committed a total of Rs 775 crore across three Indian businesses in defence technology, precision engineering and power infrastructure.
[Financial Results this week]

[New launches and partnerships]
▪️ Kuku TV Partners with Flipkart to Bring SuperCoins Rewards to Premium Microdramas
Kuku TV has partnered with Flipkart to integrate its microdrama streaming platform with the e-commerce marketplace’s SuperCoins rewards programme. Under the partnership, users subscribing to Kuku TV through Flipkart’s SuperCoins Rewards Store can receive up to 100% of their subscription value back in SuperCoins, redeemable across Flipkart, Myntra, Cleartrip and other partner platforms. Users can also redeem existing SuperCoins for up to 30% of eligible Kuku TV subscriptions. The integration will later extend to renewals, upgrades and rewards for activities such as viewing streaks and app visits.
▪️Soha Ali Khan introduces biofortified farming across Pataudi family farms with Better Nutrition
Better Nutrition, India's first biofortified food brand, has partnered with actor and author Soha Ali Khan to introduce biofortified farming across the Pataudi family farms in Haryana. In the first phase, Soha and local farming families have planted biofortified wheat across 45 acres for the rabi season, with harvest expected in April 2027. The produce will be used in Better Nutrition's atta range. Soha has also invested in the brand and joined as its brand ambassador.
▪️ Pensionbazaar partners with Zypp Electric to bring NPS to gig workers
Pensionbazaar, a brand under Paisabazaar, has partnered with EV-as-a-service platform Zypp Electric to offer National Pension System (NPS) solutions to its gig delivery partners. Under the partnership, eligible partners can digitally enrol in NPS and make flexible contributions through UPI, net banking or cards. Zypp aims to bring 60-70% of its eligible delivery partners into the pension ecosystem within 6-12 months. The initiative seeks to address retirement planning challenges among gig workers, who often face irregular incomes and limited access to traditional employee benefits.
[News flash this week]
▪️ Madras High Court issues notice on plea seeking cancellation of CULT trademark ahead of Cult.fit IPO
The Madras High Court has issued notice on a petition filed by Deepak Poduval, co-founder of the original CULT fitness business, seeking cancellation of the CULT trademark registered in the name of Cult.fit’s subsidiary, Cultfit Healthcare Pvt Ltd. The petition alleges that the 2017 assignment deeds through which the brand was transferred contain forged signatures. The court has listed the matter for 2 December 2026. Separately, Cult.fit acknowledged in its response to SEBI that its draft IPO prospectus incorrectly disclosed the ownership of the CULT trademarks, which are held by its subsidiary rather than Cult.fit Ltd, and said it would correct the disclosure in its final prospectus.
▪️ Kunal Shah sets three priorities for WhatsApp, but spam and payments remain key challenges
WhatsApp is looking to expand beyond messaging into services such as bill payments, financial services and bookings, with global head Kunal Shah outlining three priorities: richer communication, simpler services and artificial intelligence (AI). The company plans to improve features such as voice notes and video while working with financial and telecom partners to simplify everyday activities. However, WhatsApp Pay has struggled to gain traction in India, accounting for just 0.8% of UPI transaction volume in September 2026. The expansion also comes amid growing concerns over spam, with 96% of WhatsApp users receiving promotional or spam messages daily, according to a LocalCircles survey.
▪️ Kissht parent OnEMI completes Rs 832 Cr preferential issue
OnEMI Technology Solutions, the parent company of Kissht, has completed its Rs 832.20 crore preferential issue by allotting 2.64 crore shares to 34 investors, including 24 new investors and 10 existing shareholders. The new investors include Axis Mutual Fund, 360 ONE, Bandhan Small Cap Fund and MIT. Following the allotment, the newly issued shares account for around 13% of the company's expanded equity capital.
▪️ Festive boost: D2C startups bag every third funding deal in October
Indian D2C startups raised around $200 million in October, accounting for nearly 30% of the $678 million raised by startups during the month, despite a broader funding slowdown. The segment also accounted for 36 of the 108 deals, or 33.3%, compared with 21.57% in Q3 2026 and 20.36% in H1 2026. During the first nine months of 2026, D2C startups raised over $1 billion, nearly 10% of the total startup funding. Investments spanned fashion, beauty, food, wellness, lifestyle and home brands, with fresh capital expected to support inventory, distribution and marketing ahead of the festive and wedding seasons.
▪️ MeitY examines data collection by home services platforms for physical AI training
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has raised concerns over home services platforms collecting first-person video and sensor data from gig workers to train physical AI models. The ministry held a meeting with Pronto, Snabbit and Urban Company, along with technology and robotics firms, to discuss workers' consent, consumer privacy and data sovereignty. While Pronto has introduced in-home video recording through its Verified service, Snabbit and Urban Company have ruled out the practice. MeitY has sought details on data collection, storage, sharing and transfer policies, and asked Pronto to submit a detailed representation on its practices and safeguards.
▪️Paytm shares near IPO price amid MDR rollout and 6 consecutive profitable quarters
Shares of One 97 Communications, Paytm’s parent, have gained nearly 7.7% over the past two trading sessions, touching a fresh 52-week high of Rs 1,960 on Friday, and are now trading at Rs 1,939.70, around 9.8% below their IPO price of Rs 2,150. The recovery, which has more than doubled the stock from its March 2026 low of Rs 930.60, comes amid six consecutive profitable quarters and improving financial performance. Further upside could be supported by the RBI’s in-principle approval for its wallet business and the expected introduction of a 40 bps MDR on eligible UPI merchant transactions, which could open up an additional revenue stream and improve monetisation of its payments business.
